Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11

Interface CompositedWindowSink

All Known Implementing Classes:
SwingCompositedWindowSink
public interface CompositedWindowSink
The presentation end of the compositor's shared pixel pipeline: something that shows a freshly-read region of a redirected client window.

Two sinks consume the one WindowPixelSource readback:

  • the 3D sink, which uploads the pixels into a NativeWindow3D texture (the existing CompositeWindowImageLoader.updateRegion(org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.TiledNativeWindowImage, int, int, int, int, org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.fws.WindowContents) tile path);
  • the 2D sink, which paints the pixels into a Swing component hosted inside the 2D desktop, so a native X11 application appears inside a Desktop2DWindow rather than escaping as a separate top-level window.

A sink never performs X round-trips itself; CompositedWindowPipeline reads the pixels on the window-manager event thread and hands the decoded region here. Implementations that must marshal to another thread (e.g. the Swing EDT) do so inside present(java.awt.image.BufferedImage, int, int, int, int).

  • Method Details

    • present

      void present(BufferedImage region, int x, int y, int width, int height)
      Presents a freshly-read region of the window.
      Parameters:
      region - the decoded pixels, exactly width×height
      x - region left within the window, in pixels
      y - region top within the window, in pixels
      width - region width, in pixels
      height - region height, in pixels

    • resized

      default void resized(int width, int height)
      Notifies the sink that the window's full size changed, so it can resize its backing surface before the next present(java.awt.image.BufferedImage, int, int, int, int). The default is a no-op for sinks that infer size from each presented region.
      Parameters:
      width - the new window width, in pixels
      height - the new window height, in pixels

    • dispose

      default void dispose()
      Releases any resources held by the sink (e.g. removes a Swing component or frees a texture). Safe to call once when the window is unmapped or the compositor shuts down. The default is a no-op.
